title: Railway Reform, Counterfactuals, and Public Value
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
In April 1987, Japanese National Railways was replaced by six regional passenger companies and one nationwide freight company, together with related institutions for assets and liabilities. The change is commonly called privatization, but that word compresses a bundle of reforms: organizational division, debt allocation, workforce restructuring, new management incentives, and continuing public rules for an interconnected railway.

Supporters point to improved service frequency, customer orientation, traffic growth in important markets, and stronger finances at several companies. These outcomes matter, but ownership is not their only possible cause. Economic conditions, urban demand, technology, property income, debt treatment, regulation, and managerial change also varied. A before-and-after comparison therefore shows change, not the isolated effect of privatization.

The distribution of outcomes was uneven. Dense metropolitan networks and high-speed routes offered revenue opportunities that sparsely populated regions could not reproduce. Funds created to stabilize smaller regional companies acknowledge this structural difference. Through-ticketing and coordinated timetables helped preserve network value across company borders, while local lines continued to raise questions about subsidies, replacement transport, and who should pay for access.

A serious evaluation needs a counterfactual and several objectives. What reform, regulation, or investment might have occurred without the 1987 package? How should gains in productivity be weighed against employment disruption, inherited debt, rural mobility, safety, and long-term maintenance? The best conclusion may be conditional: the reform changed incentives and enabled important improvements, but its results depended on complementary institutions and geography. Public value cannot be read from profit alone.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Profit is the only valid measure of railway reform.

options.label: B
options.text: The 1987 reform was only a change in legal ownership.

options.label: C
options.text: The reform should be evaluated as a policy bundle with uneven outcomes and multiple public objectives.

options.label: D
options.text: Regional geography had no effect on railway finance.

questions.answer: 正解：C。本文は民営化を複数措置の束として扱い、地域差、反実仮想、利益以外の公共目的を含めて評価します。A・B・Dは中心的な区別を消しています。

questions.prompt: Which list contains three components that the passage separates from the single label “privatization”?

options.label: A
options.text: Regional division, debt allocation, and workforce restructuring

options.label: B
options.text: Identical geography, unchanged demand, and automatic debt cancellation

options.label: C
options.text: Only a new company name, logo, and ticket color

options.label: D
options.text: The removal of all public rules, timetables, and connections

questions.answer: 正解：A。本文は地域分割、債務配分、労働再編に加え、経営誘因と接続を維持する公共ルールを挙げます。B～Dは本文にない自動性や制度撤廃へ単純化しています。

questions.prompt: The phrase “compresses a bundle of reforms” most nearly means

options.label: A
options.text: hides several distinct changes inside one convenient label

options.label: B
options.text: physically shortens every railway line

options.label: C
options.text: cancels all inherited debt automatically

options.label: D
options.text: requires identical management in every region

questions.answer: 正解：A。一語のprivatizationが、組織・債務・雇用・誘因・規則という別々の変更をまとめて隠すという意味です。Bは比喩の誤読、C・Dは本文にない結果です。

questions.prompt: Why can a before-and-after comparison not identify the isolated effect of privatization?

options.label: A
options.text: Demand, economic conditions, technology, debt treatment, regulation, and management changed too, and the no-reform outcome is unobserved.

options.label: B
options.text: Nothing except legal ownership changed during the period.

options.label: C
options.text: A before-and-after comparison automatically creates a randomized control group.

options.label: D
options.text: Observed change can always be attributed entirely to ownership.

questions.answer: 正解：A。同時に複数要因が変わり、改革がなかった場合という反実仮想を直接観察できないため、差を所有形態だけへ帰属できません。B～Dは交絡と比較対象の欠如を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why should identical financial outcomes not be expected across metropolitan and sparsely populated regions?

options.label: A
options.text: Population density, travel demand, route costs, property opportunities, and high-speed connections create different revenue and cost structures.

options.label: B
options.text: Every region has the same ridership and property income.

options.label: C
options.text: Management effort is the only possible source of regional differences.

options.label: D
options.text: Sparse regions necessarily have more profitable high-speed routes.

questions.answer: 正解：A。人口密度、需要、路線費用、不動産収入、高速路線への接続が異なり、同じ運賃や努力でも収支構造は同じになりません。B～Dは本文の構造的地域差を否定・逆転します。

questions.prompt: Why did through-ticketing remain important after the companies were divided?

options.label: A
options.text: It preserved part of the passenger value of a connected national network.

options.label: B
options.text: It made every company legally identical.

options.label: C
options.text: It removed the need for coordinated timetables.

options.label: D
options.text: It guaranteed that no local line would ever close.

questions.answer: 正解：A。会社境界を越えて移動できる通し発券は、分割後も全国ネットワークの利用価値を保ちました。Bは法人差を消さず、Cは協調ダイヤと逆、Dは地方線存続まで保証しません。

questions.prompt: Which set consists entirely of evaluation objectives beyond profit?

options.label: A
options.text: Safety, rural mobility, long-term maintenance, and employment disruption

options.label: B
options.text: Share price, profit margin, property income, and traffic revenue only

options.label: C
options.text: Identical geography, automatic debt removal, and uniform demand

options.label: D
options.text: Ownership labels without service or access outcomes

questions.answer: 正解：A。本文は安全、地方の移動可能性、長期保守、雇用、継承債務、接続性などを利益と並べて評価します。Bは利益系指標だけ、C・Dは実在する公共目的を捉えません。

questions.prompt: What does the statement “Public value cannot be read from profit alone” imply for railway evaluation?

options.label: A
options.text: Access to schools and hospitals, regional connections, safety, resilience, and environmental effects may matter even when they are not fully reflected in revenue.

options.label: B
options.text: Operating costs and revenues should never be measured.

options.label: C
options.text: Every loss-making line must be preserved forever without comparison.

options.label: D
options.text: A profitable railway automatically maximizes all social benefits.

questions.answer: 正解：A。公共価値には通学・通院、地域間接続、安全、災害時の代替性、環境負荷など市場収入に完全には表れない便益があります。B・Cは財務評価を全面否定し、Dは利益を唯一の尺度にします。

questions.prompt: Which framework best supports a decision about maintaining or replacing a local railway?

options.label: A
options.text: Compare ridership, safety, maintenance, access, emissions, subsidy per passenger, and realistic alternatives, then assign costs and measurable targets over a defined period.

options.label: B
options.text: Close the line immediately whenever operating profit is negative.

options.label: C
options.text: Continue unlimited support without measuring service, access, or alternatives.

options.label: D
options.text: Consider only the operator's profit and ignore national, regional, and local beneficiaries.

questions.answer: 正解：A。需要、安全、維持費、生活アクセス、環境、利用者当たり補助と、バス等の現実的代替を比較し、費用分担・期限・成果目標を定めます。B～Dは単一指標か無条件継続で判断します。
